heroHeadline: Kohat Mosque Bombing Toll Rises to 31 as Taliban Spokesman's 'Crushing Response' Warning Draws Pakistani Rebuke
heroSubtitle: September 20, 2026 is Day 9,114 since the US launched Operation Enduring Freedom and Day 208 of Pakistan's Operation Ghazab lil-Haq. The death toll from the September 18 Kohat Police Lines mosque bombing rose to 31 — 16 police officers, 7 civilians and all 8 attackers — after Pakistani security forces ended a 22-hour clearance operation on September 19; more than 100 people were wounded. Ittihad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, a Hafiz Gul Bahadur-linked TTP faction, claimed responsibility. The attack triggered a sharp war of words: Taliban spokesman Zabihullah Mujahid warned Pakistan of a 'crushing response' should it strike inside Afghan territory, prompting Pakistan's Ministry of Information to call the remarks 'reprehensible' and declare Islamabad has 'both the will and the capability to eliminate terrorist threats wherever they are.' The bombing caps a bloody stretch: ISPR reported 10 militants killed in North Waziristan and Hangu between September 15-17 alongside a convoy IED that killed 6 soldiers, 9 Fitna al-Hindustan militants killed in Mastung and Pishin, Balochistan on September 14, and 7 more in Panjgur and Kachhi on September 18. Separately, Taliban Justice Minister Abdul Hakim Sharei detained Afghanistan's Supreme Shia Council head Mohammad Ali Akhlaqi and four members in a Ministry of Justice 'private prison' in Kabul on September 13. No formal ceasefire or new Urumqi round has been confirmed.
